project.name: WIZNET-PICO-C
project.description: WIZnet Ethernet chip (W5100S/W5500/W6100/W6300) test and application lab on Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico2. Targeting W6300_EVB_PICO2 with QSPI_QUAD_MODE. Includes hardware porting code, network examples, OPC UA server, and Telegram/OpenAI AI agent.

nodes.name: wiz_claw.h
nodes.summary: Core shared header for the wiz-claw AI agent library, defining common error codes (wiz_claw_err_t), overridable logging macros (WIZ_CLAW_LOG_I/W/E), and the heap string formatting utility wiz_claw_dup_printf. Has no external project-internal dependencies, making it the foundational base included by all other wiz-claw headers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses standard C only (stddef.h, stdint.h, stdbool.h, stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, stdarg.h) with no ESP-IDF or Pico SDK dependencies, making it portable across build environments. Logging macros are designed to be overridden via #ifndef guards.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_dup_printf
nodes.summary: Heap-allocates a formatted string using vsnprintf with a two-pass approach (first pass to compute required size, second pass to fill the buffer), returning a caller-owned char pointer or NULL on failure.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_http.h
nodes.summary: HTTP/1.1 client interface header for the wiz-claw library, declaring low-level TCP helpers (connect, close, send, recv) and high-level HTTP callback functions compatible with LLM and Telegram transport function pointer signatures. Defines socket number assignments and configurable buffer size constants for header and body data.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses function-pointer-based transport injection pattern: wiz_claw_http_post_cb and wiz_claw_http_call_cb can be assigned directly to wiz_claw_llm_config_t.http_post and wiz_claw_tg_config_t.http_call respectively, enabling clean separation of HTTP transport from protocol logic.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_net.h
nodes.summary: Network initialization, DNS resolution, and DHCP helper header for the wiz-claw library, wrapping ioLibrary_Driver's DNS and DHCP modules with wiz-claw error types. Declares configuration struct and API functions for DNS lookup, DHCP lease acquisition, and the required 1-second periodic tick handler.
nodes.languageNotes: Depends on ioLibrary_Driver's wizchip_conf.h for the wiz_NetInfo type; must be called after wizchip_initialize() and network_initialize(). The wiz_claw_net_1s_tick() function must be wired into a 1-second timer ISR or polling loop.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_telegram.h
nodes.summary: Telegram Bot API client interface header defining types and function declarations for polling updates, parsing incoming messages, and sending text replies. HTTP transport is injected via the wiz_claw_http_call_fn function pointer, keeping TLS and socket concerns outside this module.
nodes.languageNotes: The wiz_claw_tg_message_t struct uses a heap-allocated text field requiring explicit wiz_claw_tg_message_free() cleanup. The polling offset (inout_next_offset) follows the Telegram long-polling pattern of tracking update_id+1 to avoid reprocessing.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_tls.h
nodes.summary: mbedTLS client interface header for the wiz-claw library, providing a TLS session context struct (wiz_claw_tls_t) that wraps mbedTLS entropy, CTR-DRBG, SSL, and X.509 certificate objects alongside a WIZnet socket number. Declares the full TLS lifecycle API: init, connect, write, read, close, and free.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses RP2350 hardware TRNG (pico/rand.h get_rand_32()) as the entropy source for CTR-DRBG. The wiz_claw_tls_t struct (~1-2 KB) is explicitly documented as too large for stack allocation and should be declared as a global or static variable. CA bundle loading is conditional on WIZ_CLAW_CA_BUNDLE_PEM being defined.

nodes.name: cJSON.h
nodes.summary: Vendored cJSON 1.7.18 library header defining the core JSON node structure, type constants, memory hook typedefs, and the full public API (~60 function declarations) for parsing, serializing, and manipulating JSON trees on embedded targets.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a CJSON_PUBLIC(type) macro to handle __declspec(dllexport/import) on Windows and GCC visibility attributes on POSIX, enabling the same header to be used for both shared-library and static builds.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_agent.h
nodes.summary: Agent loop interface header that defines the tool-handler callback typedef, agent configuration struct (LLM config, system prompt, tool JSON, handler, max iterations), and the single-turn entry point wiz_claw_agent_run() which drives the LLM → tool-call → re-invoke loop.

nodes.name: wiz_claw_llm.h
nodes.summary: LLM client interface header for an OpenAI-compatible chat API, declaring the HTTP POST callback typedef, tool-call and response structs, client configuration struct, the wiz_claw_llm_chat() function, and conversation-history session helpers (create, append user/assistant/tool messages).

nodes.name: opcua_server.c
nodes.summary: Implements the open62541-based OPC UA server lifecycle and address space for the EVB-PICO2: configures server identity and endpoint URL, builds a namespace-1 node tree with live sensor data variables, and polls the server iterate loop alongside the TCP probe.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses open62541 UA_Server data-source callbacks (UA_Server_addDataSourceVariableNode) so OPC UA reads are satisfied by calling data_table_snapshot at read time rather than pushing values.

nodes.name: opcua_server_init
nodes.summary: Allocates and configures the UA_Server with a minimal custom buffer, sets server identity and URL, starts up the server, populates the address space, and launches the TCP probe.

nodes.name: opcua_server_poll
nodes.summary: Drives one iteration of the OPC UA server event loop and polls the TCP probe for new connections.

nodes.name: opcua_server_print_status
nodes.summary: Prints the current OPC UA server state, endpoint URL, status text, and delegates TCP probe status printing for diagnostic output.

nodes.name: opcua_tcp_probe.c
nodes.summary: Implements a lightweight WIZnet-socket TCP listener that decodes the OPC UA binary HEL/ACK handshake on port 4840, tracking connection statistics and endpoint URLs for diagnostic visibility into OPC UA client connections before the main server processes them.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses the OPC UA Binary Transport protocol (MessageType, ChunkType, MessageSize) directly from the TCP byte stream using little-endian read/write helpers, operating independently of the open62541 stack.

nodes.name: poll_socket
nodes.summary: State machine polling a WIZnet socket through CLOSED/OPENED/LISTENING/ESTABLISHED states, receiving data and dispatching to process_rx for OPC UA handshake parsing.

nodes.name: process_rx
nodes.summary: Parses an OPC UA binary transport frame from the receive buffer, recognizing HEL and OpenSecureChannel message types and dispatching ACK or error responses accordingly.

nodes.name: opcua_tcp_probe_init
nodes.summary: Zeroes the probe state, closes any existing socket, and prints initialization status.

nodes.name: opcua_tcp_probe_poll
nodes.summary: Checks network readiness and, if the link is down, closes the probe socket; otherwise drives poll_socket for one iteration.

nodes.name: usb_stdio_link.c

nodes.name: process_line

nodes.name: usb_stdio_link_poll

nodes.name: can.c
nodes.summary: Complete software CAN 2.0B controller implementation (can2040) for the RP2040/RP2350, using PIO state machines for bit-level timing, hardware-accelerated bit stuffing/unstuffing, CRC computation, and interrupt-driven frame reception and transmission.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the full CAN 2.0B protocol stack in software on top of RP2040 PIO peripherals; uses GCC builtins (__builtin_clz, __builtin_bswap32) and ARM DMB memory barriers for correctness on Cortex-M0+.

nodes.name: can2040_pio_irq_handler
nodes.summary: PIO IRQ handler that dispatches incoming CAN bus events (RX data, ACK done, line matched, may-TX, TX pending) to the appropriate report handlers.

nodes.name: can2040_transmit
nodes.summary: Encodes a CAN frame (standard or extended ID, data payload) with bit stuffing and CRC into the TX queue and triggers PIO transmission.

nodes.name: can2040_start
nodes.summary: Starts the can2040 controller by resetting data state, initializing PIO hardware, and entering the initial discard state.

nodes.name: can2040_setup
nodes.summary: Initialises a can2040 state structure with a given PIO number, zeroing all fields and recording the PIO base address.

nodes.name: pio_setup
nodes.summary: Configures all four PIO state machines (sync, RX, match, TX) for CAN bus timing, sets clock dividers, and assigns GPIO pins to PIO functions.

nodes.name: process_rx
nodes.summary: Processes a raw PIO RX word by feeding bits through the unstuffer and data state machine, handling passive and error conditions.

nodes.name: can.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the can2040 software CAN controller, declaring the can2040 state struct, can2040_msg frame type, statistics struct, and the public API (setup, start, stop, transmit, check_transmit, callback_config, get_statistics, pio_irq_handler).

nodes.languageNotes: PIO assembly for the RP2040 programmable I/O subsystem; each program handles a specific phase of the CAN protocol (sync detection, bit reception, frame matching, bit transmission).

nodes.name: wiznet_spi_pio_open

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The root README is your map for everything that follows. It defines the project's goals — verifying W5100S through W6300 chips — and names the target board (W6300_EVB_PICO2 in QSPI_QUAD_MODE), the six example programs, and the four port-layer subsystems. Reading it first lets you understand why each directory exists before you encounter a single line of C code.

tour.title: Build System Entry Point
tour.description: The top-level CMakeLists.txt is the single source of truth for how the entire project gets compiled. It selects the target board, bootstraps the Pico SDK, pins the WIZnet SDK version via wiznet_pico_c_sdk_version.cmake, and then delegates to the port and examples sub-trees. Understanding this file shows you which compile-time switches control SPI vs. QSPI mode and how the SDK import chain is structured.
tour.languageLesson: CMake uses add_subdirectory() to compose a project from separate CMakeLists.txt files. The top-level file sets cache variables (e.g., BOARD_NAME) that child CMakeLists inherit, making it the authoritative place to change build-wide settings.

tour.title: Submodule Dependencies
tour.description: The .gitmodules file declares five Git submodules — pico-sdk, ioLibrary_Driver, mbedtls, open62541, and can2040 — that provide every third-party library this project depends on. Each submodule is a pinned commit, so the build is reproducible. This is the dependency manifest equivalent of a package.json for embedded C: change a pin here and the entire third-party tree shifts.
tour.languageLesson: Git submodules embed a foreign repository at a specific commit. Running 'git submodule update --init --recursive' after cloning fetches all five at their pinned SHAs. The libraries/CMakeLists.txt then adds them to the build graph.

tour.title: Board & Port Common Definitions
tour.description: Before any driver code can compile, the project needs to know which physical board it targets. board_list.h defines preprocessor symbols for every supported WIZnet Pico variant, and port_common.h provides the shared portability macros and type aliases (u8, u16, etc.) that all hardware drivers use. Together these two headers form the lowest-level vocabulary the rest of the port layer speaks.
tour.languageLesson: Embedded C projects use header-only board selection: a #define like BOARD_W6300_EVB_PICO2 is set in the CMake toolchain file, and every driver file guards its pin assignments with #ifdef blocks, keeping one codebase that compiles correctly for any board variant.

tour.title: Hardware Abstraction Layer: SPI & QSPI Drivers
tour.description: The heart of the Hardware Abstraction Layer is the SPI/QSPI port in port/ioLibrary_Driver. wizchip_spi.c and wizchip_spi.h implement the standard SPI callback that the WIZnet ioLibrary calls for every register read/write. wizchip_qspi_pio.c and wizchip_qspi_pio.pio take this further, using the RP2040/RP2350 PIO state machines to implement quad-SPI transfers at hardware speed. This is what makes the W6300 in QSPI_QUAD_MODE possible on the Pico platform.
tour.languageLesson: PIO (Programmable I/O) programs are written in a custom assembly language (.pio files) and compiled by pioasm into C header arrays. The CPU loads the program into a state machine, which then runs bit-banging loops at clock speed, independent of the CPU — allowing precise timing that standard GPIO cannot achieve.

tour.title: Hardware Abstraction Layer: Timer & GPIO IRQ
tour.description: Two supporting HAL components complete the chip interface picture. timer.h and timer.c implement a 1 ms repeating hardware timer that the ioLibrary uses for DHCP timeouts, ARP retries, and other protocol bookkeeping — without it, TCP/IP stacks would stall waiting for timed events. wizchip_gpio_irq.c provides the interrupt callback wiring that allows the chip's INT pin to wake the MCU instead of polling the chip status register in a busy loop.

tour.title: Network Test Examples
tour.description: With the HAL in place, the four network examples in the examples/ directory systematically verify the chip. WIZnet_Chip_Buffer_Test.c stress-tests the TX buffer with write-readback patterns to confirm memory integrity. PING_TEST.c sends ICMP echo requests to verify basic IP connectivity. wizchip_loopback.c exercises both TCP and UDP in a server/client loop. 10M_Complience_Test.c drives the PHY through the IEEE 802.3 10 Mbit/s compliance test waveforms. Together they form a graduated confidence ladder from register-level sanity to full protocol validation.

tour.title: Protocol Adaptation: OPC UA Port
tour.description: The OPC UA stack (open62541) expects a POSIX-style BSD socket API, but WIZnet chips use their own ioLibrary socket calls. The Protocol Adaptation Layer bridges this gap. port/open62541/lwip/sockets.h provides the BSD socket shim that maps POSIX calls to WIZnet equivalents, and open62541_wiznet_eventloop.c replaces open62541's default libuv event loop with one that drives the WIZnet socket state machine. Without this glue, open62541 would be impossible to run on bare-metal Pico hardware.
tour.languageLesson: open62541 is designed to be portable via its 'event loop' abstraction. By replacing the default event loop implementation, you can run the OPC UA stack on any transport — WIZnet sockets, lwIP, or bare POSIX — without modifying the open62541 library itself.

tour.title: OPC UA Application: Data Flow
tour.description: The opcua_usb_stdio example is a multi-module application that bridges sensor data arriving over USB CDC into an OPC UA server accessible over Ethernet. data_table.h and data_table.c define the central shared data structure — a DataTable — that all modules read and write. usb_stdio_link.c parses ASCII frames from the USB serial port and populates the DataTable. opcua_server.c then reads from the same DataTable and exposes its values as OPC UA nodes defined by opcua_node_map.h.

tour.title: OPC UA Application: Server & Network Lifecycle
tour.description: Building on the DataTable from Step 9, opcua_server.c implements the full open62541 server lifecycle: node registration, variable callback binding, and the iterate loop that drives the OPC UA protocol engine. opcua_tcp_probe.c handles the low-level OPC UA HEL/ACK TCP handshake needed before open62541 takes over the connection. wiznet_network.c manages the WIZnet chip's network lifecycle — DHCP lease acquisition, link-up detection, and reconnection — while the top-level main.c orchestrates the polling loop that ticks all subsystems together.
tour.languageLesson: OPC UA uses a binary TCP transport. The client opens a TCP connection and sends a HEL (Hello) message; the server responds with ACK before the OPC UA session negotiation begins. opcua_tcp_probe.c handles this initial handshake so that open62541 receives an already-established connection.

tour.title: AI Agent Library: Core Interfaces
tour.description: The wiz-claw library (port/wiz-claw) is a portable embedded AI agent framework. wiz_claw.h is the core shared header that every other module includes for common types and configuration. wiz_claw_net.h and wiz_claw_net.c handle WIZnet-specific network initialization, DHCP, and DNS resolution. wiz_claw_tls.h and wiz_claw_tls.c wrap mbedTLS around WIZnet sockets to produce a TLS channel, backed by the embedded CA certificate bundle in wiz_claw_ca_bundle.h that validates Telegram and OpenAI server certificates without a filesystem.
tour.languageLesson: Embedded TLS without a filesystem requires the CA certificate bundle to be compiled into flash as a C array. gen_ca_bundle.py (port/wiz-claw/tools) runs at development time to fetch Mozilla's CA bundle and emit a wiz_claw_ca_bundle.h header, which wiz_claw_tls.c passes directly to mbedTLS as a trusted root store.

tour.title: AI Agent Library: HTTP, LLM & Telegram
tour.description: With TLS established, wiz_claw_http.c provides an HTTP/1.1 client that runs over WIZnet sockets and can switch to TLS via the wiz_claw_tls layer. wiz_claw_llm.c builds on the HTTP client to implement an OpenAI-compatible chat completion API — it serializes the request to JSON using cJSON, POSTs it over HTTPS, and parses the streamed response. wiz_claw_telegram.c similarly uses the HTTP client to poll the Telegram Bot API for new messages and to send replies. cJSON.h and cJSON.c provide the vendored JSON library all three modules share.

tour.title: AI Agent Example: Top-Level Application
tour.description: The wiz_claw_agent example is the complete showcase of every layer in this codebase. wiz_claw_agent.h and wiz_claw_agent.c implement the agent loop that orchestrates the full cycle: receive a Telegram message, forward it to the OpenAI LLM, parse any tool-call responses, execute the requested GPIO action on the Pico's pins, and reply back to Telegram. The application's main.c wires together network initialization, agent configuration, and the polling loop. This single example exercises the HAL (GPIO), the wiz-claw network/TLS/HTTP stack, and the LLM tool-call dispatch pattern all at once.
tour.languageLesson: OpenAI tool calls (function calling) let the LLM respond with a structured JSON object that names a function and its arguments instead of free text. The embedded agent parses this JSON with cJSON, maps the function name to a GPIO action, executes it, and sends the result back to the model as a tool-result message — enabling the LLM to control physical hardware through conversation.
